Description: Continuously ingest SpO2, Heart Rate and BP from the patient's wearable, validate readings and detect threshold breaches within 2 seconds on a scalable, secure gateway.
Raise emergency alerts for critical breaches, notify the on-call caregiver within 3 seconds and escalate through the caregiver matrix reliably.
Let the on-call caregiver view alert details and acknowledge an alert in one action, stopping escalation and keeping an audit trail.
Give patients and caregivers live visibility of vitals and alerts, let caregivers configure patient thresholds, and protect health data with access control.

As a remote patient,
I want my wearable to continuously send SpO2, heart rate and BP to the system,
So that my condition is monitored without hospital visits.

As a on-call caregiver,
I want corrupted or out-of-range sensor readings to be filtered out,
So that false alarms are reduced and I can trust the alerts.

Summary: Story 1.3: Detect threshold breach within 2 s
Description:
As a on-call caregiver,
I want critical readings (e.g. HR > 140 BPM) flagged within 2 seconds,
So that I can respond before the patient deteriorates.

As a on-call caregiver,
I want the gateway to handle 500 concurrent encrypted streams at 99.99% uptime,
So that every post-operative patient is monitored reliably and securely.

As a on-call caregiver,
I want an emergency alert created with patient, metric, value and time,
So that I have the full context of the emergency.

As a on-call caregiver,
I want to receive a push and SMS within 3 seconds of a critical breach,
So that I am informed immediately even if the app is closed.

As a remote patient,
I want unacknowledged alerts escalated to the next caregiver after 60 seconds,
So that help reaches me even if the first caregiver is unreachable.

As a remote patient,
I want failed notifications retried and a voice call used as fallback,
So that no emergency alert is ever lost.

Summary: Story 3.1: Acknowledge alert in one action
Description:
As a on-call caregiver,
I want to acknowledge an alert with a single tap,
So that escalation stops and others know I am responding.

As a on-call caregiver,
I want my caregiver ID and acknowledgement time recorded,
So that there is an accountable clinical and legal record.

Summary: Story 3.3: View alert details with current vitals
Description:
As a on-call caregiver,
I want to see the patient's current vitals when I open an alert,
So that I can judge the severity and act quickly.

As a remote patient,
I want to see my own live vitals and alert status,
So that I feel reassured and informed about my recovery.

As a on-call caregiver,
I want a dashboard of live vitals for my assigned patients, refreshed every 5 s,
So that I keep situational awareness across patients.

As a on-call caregiver,
I want to set clinical thresholds per patient,
So that alerts match each patient's surgery and condition.

As a on-call caregiver,
I want to browse a patient's past alerts,
So that I can spot trends and review responses.

Summary: Story 4.5: Encrypt data and enforce access control
Description:
As a remote patient,
I want my health data encrypted and visible only to authorised caregivers,
So that my privacy is protected.
